title.from: Public pages that make the newsroom visible: section fronts, Reference grids and Message threads mixed with Stories (working id: wire)
title.to: Home page: public section fronts, Reference grids and Message threads mixed with Stories, on every Papyrus site

description.from:
Ryan, 2026-10-31: standard, reusable public pages that make parts of the newsroom visible to site visitors, deployable on any Papyrus site from one implementation (DRY, configured per site, off by default). Tested on Anth.us first, as a NEW section at https://anth.us/newsroom (Anth.us's own segment and label: "newsroom"; the CMS console stays at https://newsroom.anth.us). Anth.us's existing home page and landing pages do not change.

## Working identifier: `wire` (placeholder, to be renamed)

Ryan has not named the feature. Every ticket here uses the neutral working identifier `wire` for the settings key (`projection.json` `"wire"`), the data directory (`_data/wire/`), the Python modules (`src/papyrus_content/wire/`, `projection/standard/wire*.py`), the projection task (`wire-snapshot`) and the backend plugin (`amplify/plugins/wire/`). "Newsroom" is NOT the feature name: it is only Anth.us's URL segment and label. Do not use "newsroom" in identifiers, settings keys or docs for this feature, so implementers never confuse it with the CMS newsroom (`newsroomBasePath`, `newsroom.anth.us`, the `/newsroom*` CMS edge route). A rename to Ryan's chosen name is one mechanical chore before the docs task (PPY docs task in this epic names it).

## What ships (phases, each visible on Anth.us when it lands)

1. Wire snapshot: a projection task writes public JSON data files of accepted and recommended References under `_data/wire/`, with an allowlist of fields and the reader-privacy scan (child task: snapshot).
2. `::include{kind="references" ...}`: Reference grids with three selections (recent accepted, most confident accepted, most confident not yet accepted), rendered at projection time from the snapshot, with page-level de-duplication (child task: references include).
3. Anth.us opt-in: `pages[]` entry at path `newsroom` with an authored Markus file interleaving Story listings and Reference grids; Markdown twin and llms.txt entry come from the standard front end; a read-only edge check (child tasks: Anth.us section, edge check).
4. Freshness: DynamoDB streams on Reference (and later Message) tables -> debounce -> `wire-snapshot` task -> re-render only the pages whose inputs changed (child task: freshness).
5. Section index pages and a home page of section blocks, as standard front-end settings, generalising Shipped's section landing hook and the default listing page (child task: section fronts).
6. Message threads, read-only: `_data/wire/threads.json` plus `::include{kind="threads" ...}` list/grid (child task: threads). Blocked on Ryan's author-display decision (open question 2).
7. p.apyr.us docs (child task: docs).

A separate P3 epic stub holds the future direction (forum-style thread pages that anyone can read, posting by signed-in visitors, interactive publications, public Reference curation as on Shipped). Not in scope here; the seams are listed below.

## Design decisions and reasons

### Extend, don't fork
- Home-of-sections and section index pages become settings of the standard front end (`home.layout`, `urls.sections.<name>.index`), implemented in `projection/standard/projector.py` next to the existing home and listing pages. Shipped's `main(page)` landing (tabs, label, description, lead story, latest list, older link) is the model; TI's showcase bands and p.apyr.us's section descriptions and nav are the other inputs. No site keeps a private copy afterwards; Shipped may drop its hook later (separate site PR).
- The layout model is the authored page file that already exists: `pages[].source` Markdown with `::band`, `::include{kind="listing"}` and the new `::include{kind="references"}` / `::include{kind="threads"}` directives, in document order. No new JSON layout schema. "Slots" are just directive order; a feature Story, a panel of References, more Stories, a list of lists, more References is one Markdown file. Section index pages get a default generated layout (the Shipped landing shape) and may be replaced by an authored file with `urls.sections.<name>.index.source`.
- Story selection uses the existing `listing` include, which already takes `sections=`, `tags=`, `count`, `skip`, `card=`; it is type-agnostic (any `listings.types`). Nothing here says "article" or "post".
- Reference rendering reuses the knowledge-blocks pattern (`knowledge.py` `KnowledgeSource` + `knowledge_blocks.py`): a `WireSource` reads `_data/wire/*.json` from the store (or a local directory), the page digest folds the snapshot digest in (`_shared()` / `_knowledge_inputs()` pattern), and reconcile never deletes `_data/wire/` (`PLUGIN_RUNTIME_DIRECTORIES`).

### Data flow
Reference, MessageThread and Message are readable only by the editor/admin groups and the backend's IAM functions; nothing public reads them today. Projection renders from PublishedItem only. So:
1. The `wire-snapshot` projection task (content-actions, `run_projection_task`, same place as `reader-snapshot`) reads, with the IAM authoring client: References by `referencesByCurationStatusKey` (`<corpusId>#accepted`), `referencesByFeedStateAndPrediction` (`<corpusId>#unrated`, read fully, sorted locally; `list_by_index` is ascending only), the current `relevance_decision_is` SemanticRelation per lineage (`semanticRelationsBySubjectState`, for the live confidence), and `ReferenceAttachment` `role: "preview"` for image and description.
2. It writes `_data/wire/references.json` (allowlisted public fields only; see privacy) under the site's URL policy (`policy.key`, so `urls.basePath` is honoured), under the projection lease, only when the content minus `generatedAt` changed.
3. It then calls `project_listings(context)` so only pages whose digest includes the changed wire digest are rewritten (the include records which selections a page uses; the digest is per selection file, so a change in pending References does not rewrite a page that shows only accepted ones).
4. Pages are server-rendered HTML (SEO, no-JS, `.md` twins); the JSON files are public too so a later client component can refresh them without a page rebuild (seam for the Web 2.0 direction). No client fetching is built now.

### Freshness strategy (decision)
Chosen: event-driven, debounced re-snapshot plus incremental listing re-render; optional periodic safety run; no edge purge by default.
- Trigger: a DynamoDB stream (NEW_IMAGE) on the Reference table, consumed by a small `wire-trigger` Lambda that ignores records whose `curationStatus`/`feedStateKey`/`predictionSortKey` did not change, then claims a trailing-edge debounce slot (conditional put on the projection lock table, pk `wire-debounce#<bucket>`) and creates a one-off EventBridge Scheduler schedule (`ActionAfterCompletion: DELETE`) that invokes content-actions with `{"projectionTask": {"task": "wire-snapshot"}}`. This is the reader-steering debounce pattern (`amplify/plugins/reader-steering/papyrus.plugin.ts`, `function/handler.py` `claim_snapshot_slot`) and the Message stream wiring already in `amplify/site-backend.ts` (`streamSpecification` on the Message cfn table). One trigger covers every writer: human votes (`reviewReferenceCuration`), `auto_accept`, `auto_reject`, the router's `record_original_prediction`, and later `postMessage`, without touching any of them.
- Why not re-project on every accept: auto-accept and monitor runs accept in bursts; one snapshot per window is the same freshness at a fraction of the cost.
- Why not periodic only: idle sites would pay for empty runs and busy sites would be stale for the whole interval. A periodic rule stays available as a safety net (`wire.freshness.intervalHours`, off by default), the same shape as `snapshot.schedule` in reader-steering.
- Why not JSON + client-side rendering only: invisible to search engines and agents, nothing without JavaScript, and the `.md` twin would be empty. The JSON files are still published for the future.
- Debounce window default 300 s, which is the HTML `s-maxage` the writers already set (`PAPYRUS_HTML_S_MAXAGE_SECONDS` default 300). With purge off, a page can never be fresher than its edge lifetime, so a shorter window buys nothing; `wire.freshness.debounceSeconds` is configurable, and `wire.freshness.purge: true` turns CloudFront invalidation on for sites that want it (cost: invalidation paths, 1000 free a month, then per path).
- Cost: one Lambda run per burst, a handful of index reads, one small S3 write, a few listing pages re-rendered. The snapshot holds every eligible Reference (accepted and current; pending with original P(accept) >= 0.5), bounded only by real limits (the Lambda's 900 s timeout and the page render); if a site's file grows past what the Lambda renders comfortably, trimming is a follow-up measured from data, not a fixed cap now.
- Deploy render and reconcile re-render pages from the snapshot already in S3 (`attach_store`, as `KnowledgeSource` does), so a deploy never blanks the grids.

### Reference selections and ranking
Terms follow the newsroom console (`lib/reference-feed-ranking.ts`, `docs/reference-feed-indexes.md`):
- `recent`: accepted (`curationStatus == accepted`, `versionState == current`), newest `curationStatusUpdatedAt` first (that is the accept time; there is no `acceptedAt`), ties by `feedArrivalAt` then public key.
- `confident`: accepted, highest confidence first, where confidence = the current `relevance_decision_is` relation's P(accept) exactly as `acceptProbability()` computes it (label vs positiveLabel, `confidence`, 0.6 when unrecorded, 0.5 when undecided), ties by `compareNewest` order. This is the console's "Best bets" comparator applied to accepted References.
- `recommended`: not accepted (`feedStateKey` `#unrated`), P(accept) >= 0.5 (the decision threshold the console already uses to skip predicted rejects; not an arbitrary number), highest first; same tie-break. Rejected and archived References are never public.
- An optional `section=` attribute filters by `curationSectionId` (set on accept), so a section index page can show its own section's References.

### Page-level de-duplication
A per-page `WireLedger` (set of public keys already placed) is created when a page render starts and passed to every `_include` call in document order. A `references` include draws candidates in its selection order, skips keys already in the ledger, and stops at `count`. The first component on the page wins; later components refill from their own ordering, so a component shows `count` items unless the pool is exhausted. The ledger is keyed `reference:<key>` so the same mechanism can later de-duplicate Stories across `listing` includes (`dedupe="true"`, follow-up) and Threads. De-duplication is per page, never across pages.

### Configuration (per site, `projection.json`; off unless `wire` is present)
```json
{
  "wire": {
    "references": {
      "corpus": "knowledge-corpus-anth-us",
      "fields": ["title", "url", "host", "sourceDate", "acceptedAt", "section", "confidence", "image", "summary", "actor"],
      "recommendedThreshold": 0.5
    },
    "threads": {"enabled": false, "authors": "none"},
    "freshness": {"debounceSeconds": 300, "intervalHours": null, "purge": false}
  },
  "home": {"layout": "sections", "perSection": 4},
  "urls": {"sections": {"articles": {"base": "articles", "label": "Articles", "description": "...", "index": {"lead": true, "latest": 12, "references": "recent"}}}}
}
```
`fields` is an allowlist chosen from the public field set; a field not listed is not written. `corpus` defaults to the site's knowledge corpus id from the site key (`ids.py`). The backend side (`papyrus.config.ts` `backend.plugins: ["wire"]`) turns on the stream, the trigger and the task; the projection side renders only what the snapshot holds, so a site may render a snapshot it maintains by CLI (`papyrus wire snapshot`) without the plugin.

### Privacy policy (public pages carry no person identity)
- References: public fields are `key` (sha256 of `lineageId`, first 12 hex, so no UUID appears), `title`, `url` (`sourceUri`), `host` (derived, `www.` stripped), `sourceDate` (`sourcePublishedAt`), `acceptedAt` (`curationStatusUpdatedAt`, accepted only), `section` (label of `curationSectionId`), `confidence` (rounded to 2 decimals), `image` and `summary` (from the `preview` attachment), `actor` (`"editor"`, `"automatic"` or absent, from `curationActorKind`; never who). Never written: `curationStatusUpdatedBy` (often an email), `curationStatusReason`, `curationDelegation`, `versionCreatedBy`, `discoveryDetails`, `discoveryRule`, any id or UUID, `authors` (open question 4).
- Threads and Messages: only threads whose anchor is public (an accepted Reference in the snapshot, or a published Story), only `status: active` Messages; deleted Messages are omitted entirely (the text stays in DynamoDB after a soft delete, so an export must drop them, as the console blanks them). `authorSub`, `createdBySub`, `authorUserProfileId`, `deletedBySub` are never written. `authorLabel` can be an email on older Messages: the display policy is open question 2; until decided, no author is shown at all.
- Every wire file and every page is checked by the existing scanner `procedures/newsroom/tests/reader_privacy.py` `identity_leaks()` in the Gherkin steps, and Shipped's live scan covers it on that site.

### Agent-readable pages
Authored pages (`pages[].source`) already get a `.md` twin and an `llms.txt` entry. The twin keeps `::include{kind="references"}` and `::include{kind="threads"}` lines as written, as it does for knowledge blocks (`blocks.twin`), because the line says what the page shows and where the data lives; the data files are public JSON next to the page. Section index pages and the sections home get twins through `add()` like every generated page.

### Edge and the `newsroom` segment (Anth.us)
- On Anth.us the public edge (`papyrus-edge-anth-us`, distribution `E3UMOOJRMY7FK7`) is pure S3: default behaviour only, 403/404 -> `/404.html`; `anth.us/newsroom` already 301s to `/newsroom/` and 404s; the KVS has no `/newsroom` key; the CMS is its own distribution (`newsroom.anth.us`). So NO edge change is needed for `anth.us/newsroom/`: writing `newsroom/index.html` to the bucket serves it. The child task "edge check" verifies this read-only and records it; any change that did turn out to be needed is its own task and needs Ryan's approval before it is applied.
- Every other site's edge (`infra/edge/s3-projection-cms.yaml`; Shipped, Distinctive Mark, Data Parade, TI) routes `/newsroom*`, `/_next/*` and `/api/*` to the CMS Amplify app, so a `pages[]` path or section base `newsroom` there would be shadowed by the CMS. That is why the segment is per-site configuration. The docs task adds this to `docs/site-hosting.md`; a build-time check is not possible (projection does not know the edge), so the standard config refuses only the reserved prefixes it does know (`_data`, `_plugins`, `_papyrus`, `_next`, `api`) and documents `newsroom` as reserved on CMS-style edges.
- Projection itself treats no segment specially: `urls.basePath`, redirects and reconcile have no `newsroom` rule (`owns_page_key` only excludes `css/`, `assets/`, `_`-prefixed keys and `_data/knowledge/`).

### Seams for the future (not built now)
- Forum view: each thread gets `_data/wire/threads/<key>.json` (messages in sequence) in the threads task, and a `threads` include links to a per-thread page path reserved as `urls.wire.threadBase` (default `conversations`); the page itself is the later epic.
- Public posting: Messages stay people-only; a public post would be a guest mutation (as reader-steering's `guest.mutations`) writing a Message with a reader identity (readerId/handle policy from reader-steering), moderated through `moderateMessage`. The export's author policy (`wire.threads.authors`) is the single place that decides what is shown.
- Interactive publications: the published JSON files plus the islands runtime (`papyrus-islands.js`, `::island{}`) are the mount points; a `wire` island reading `_data/wire/*.json` is a later task.
- Public curation (Shipped reader-steering): the `recommended` selection is the natural place for reader votes to appear; the reader plugin's `subjects.json` can gain `reference:<key>` subjects later.

## Open questions for Ryan (decisions needed, in order)

1. Feature name (replaces the working identifier `wire`; candidates):
   - "Wire": the newswire, the stream of what the newsroom took in and is considering; short, familiar press word; pairs with "Stories".
   - "Open Newsroom": says exactly what it is (the newsroom made visible) but collides with the CMS name on every other site.
   - "Backstage": what happens before publication; friendly, but hides that the content is curated References.
   - "Ledger": a public record of accepts and recommendations; honest and auditable, but dry.
   - "Dispatch": things sent out from the newsroom; evocative, but suggests newsletters.
2. Author display on public Messages: (a) none (default until decided), (b) a role word only ("Editor" / "AI"), (c) a display name the Account member opts into per site (new `publicHandle` on UserProfile). Older Messages hold emails in `authorLabel`, so (c) needs the opt-in field, not the label.
3. Is `confidence` public at all? It reveals Cyclotron's score per Reference. Options: show it (as a number plus a Lucide meter, never colour alone), show only the `recommended` ordering without the number, or hide for accepted and show for recommended.
4. Which Reference fields are public: the proposed allowlist above; in particular `authors` (source authors, not people in the Account; they are public on the source already) and `summary` (the og:description of the source page).
5. Default counts: the Anth.us page proposes 6 recent, 6 confident and 6 recommended; the sections home proposes 4 per section (two rows of two on a phone). Confirm or change; both are settings.
6. Should pending-but-recommended References be public on Anth.us at launch, or only accepted ones first (the plan ships both selections; Anth.us's page file decides which it places)?
7. Nav: does `/newsroom/` get a link in the Anth.us menu (`anthus_dom.MENU_LINKS`) at launch, or stay discoverable only from the footer and llms.txt?

## Acceptance criteria for the epic
- With configuration only, a Papyrus site shows accepted References (and optionally recommended ones and Message threads) on public pages that interleave with Story listings; each Reference appears at most once per page.
- https://anth.us/newsroom/ is live from the standard projector; Anth.us's existing pages are byte-identical apart from a nav link if Ryan wants one.
- Changes to curation reach the public pages within one debounce window plus the edge lifetime, with no per-site code.
- No public page or data file contains an email, a person id, a Cognito sub or a UUID (reader-privacy scan in CI).
- Section index pages and a home of section blocks are available to every site as settings.
- Gherkin specs (narrative, complete) for every behaviour change; p.apyr.us documents the feature.

A per-page `PageLedger` (set of public keys already placed) is created when a page render starts and passed to every `_include` call in document order. A `references` include draws candidates in its selection order, skips keys already in the ledger, and stops at `count`. The first component on the page wins; later components refill from their own ordering, so a component shows `count` items unless the pool is exhausted. The ledger is keyed `reference:<key>` so the same mechanism can later de-duplicate Stories across `listing` includes (`dedupe="true"`, follow-up) and Threads. De-duplication is per page, never across pages.

### Configuration (per site, `projection.json`; off unless `homePage` is present)
```json
{
  "homePage": {
    "layout": "sections", "perSection": 4,
    "references": {
      "corpus": "knowledge-corpus-anth-us",
      "fields": "all", "defaultCount": 6,
      "recommendedThreshold": 0.5
    },
    "threads": {"enabled": false, "authors": "handle", "anonymousLabel": "Editor"},
    "freshness": {"debounceSeconds": 300, "intervalHours": null, "purge": false}
  },
  "urls": {"sections": {"articles": {"base": "articles", "label": "Articles", "description": "...", "index": {"lead": true, "latest": 12, "references": "recent"}}}}
}
```
`fields` is `"all"` (every field in the code's public allowlist, the default) or a list chosen from that allowlist; a field not in the code allowlist is a build error. `corpus` defaults to the site's knowledge corpus id from the site key (`ids.py`). The backend side (`papyrus.config.ts` `backend.plugins: ["home-page"]`) turns on the stream, the trigger and the task; the projection side renders only what the snapshot holds, so a site may render a snapshot it maintains by CLI (`papyrus home-page snapshot`) without the plugin.

### Privacy policy (public pages carry no person identity)
Ryan, 2026-10-31: publish all Reference fields except identity, full third-party text and internal plumbing; show Cyclotron's confidence; authors on Messages are opt-in public handles.
- References: the code holds an explicit allowlist (`home_page/export.py` `PUBLIC_REFERENCE_FIELDS`), applied to every export. Published: `key` (sha256 of `lineageId`, first 12 hex, so no UUID appears), `status` (`accepted` | `recommended`), `title`, `authors` (the source's authors, already public on the source), `url` (`sourceUri`), `host` (derived), `mediaType`, `sourceDate` (`sourcePublishedAt`), `sourceUpdatedAt`, `retrievedAt`, `importedAt`, `arrivedAt` (`feedArrivalAt`), `acceptedAt` (`curationStatusUpdatedAt`, accepted only), `decidedAt` (`curationStatusUpdatedAt`), `section` (label of `curationSectionId`), `reasonCode` (`curationReasonCode`), `actor` (`curationActorKind`: `human` shown as "an editor", `cyclotron`/`rule`/`agent`/`catalog` shown as "automatically"; never who), `shareable` (`curationShareable`), `confidence` (live P(accept), 2 decimals), `predictedAcceptProbability` (the original prediction, 2 decimals), `predictionDecidedAt`, `inboundCitationCount`, `outboundCitationCount`, `versionNumber`, `image` and `summary` and `siteName` (from the `preview` attachment's `sourceUri` and `metadata`).
  Excluded, with the reason: (a) identity: `curationStatusUpdatedBy` (often an email), `versionCreatedBy`, `curationDelegation` (`relayedBy`), `curationStatusReason` (an editor's private note, may name people), `discoveryDetails` and `discoveryRule` (intake provenance, may carry email-intake addresses); (b) third-party text: no captured or extracted body, no attachment other than the preview image URL and og:description (`summary`, clipped at `publicData.summaryCharacters`, default 240), because republishing full text is a copyright risk; (c) plumbing: `id`, `lineageId`, `previousVersionId`, `corpusId`, `externalItemId`, `importRunId`, `contentHash`, `sha256`, `storagePath`, `byteSize`, `discoveredByMonitorId`, `curationDecisionRelationId`, `newsroomFeedKey`, `reviewedFeedKey`, `feedStateKey`, `predictionSortKey`, `versionState`, `curationStatusKey`. Rejected and archived References are never exported.
- Confidence is public (Ryan: show off Cyclotron): the card shows "93% confidence" as text next to a Lucide `gauge` icon and a five-segment meter whose filled segments are drawn with shape (filled vs outlined), never colour alone; the `recommended` chip says "Recommended by Cyclotron, not yet accepted" with a `sparkles` icon.
- Threads and Messages: only threads whose anchor is public (an accepted or recommended Reference in the snapshot, or a published Story), only `status: active` Messages; deleted Messages are omitted entirely (the text stays in DynamoDB after a soft delete). `authorSub`, `createdBySub`, `authorUserProfileId`, `deletedBySub`, `authorLabel`, `createdByLabel`, `metadata.lastAuthorLabel` are never written. Author display (Ryan, 2026-10-31): an opt-in public handle, `UserProfile.publicHandle`, set by the person in the console's own profile settings (task PPY handle); the export joins `authorUserProfileId` to the profile and writes `author: {"handle": "ryan"}` when one is set, otherwise `author: {"label": "Editor"}` (`homePage.threads.anonymousLabel`, or "AI" when `role != human`). A handle is 3 to 24 characters of `[a-z0-9-]`, unique per site, never containing `@`.
- Every home-page data file and every page is checked by the existing scanner `procedures/newsroom/tests/reader_privacy.py` `identity_leaks()` in the Gherkin steps (handles are not UUIDs, emails or subs, so the scan stays strict), and Shipped's live scan covers it on that site.

### Agent-readable pages
Authored pages (`pages[].source`) already get a `.md` twin and an `llms.txt` entry. The twin keeps `::include{kind="references"}` and `::include{kind="threads"}` lines as written, as it does for knowledge blocks (`blocks.twin`), because the line says what the page shows and where the data lives; the data files are public JSON next to the page. Section index pages and the sections home get twins through `add()` like every generated page.

### Edge and the `newsroom` segment (Anth.us)
- On Anth.us the public edge (`papyrus-edge-anth-us`, distribution `E3UMOOJRMY7FK7`) is pure S3: default behaviour only, 403/404 -> `/404.html`; `anth.us/newsroom` already 301s to `/newsroom/` and 404s; the KVS has no `/newsroom` key; the CMS is its own distribution (`newsroom.anth.us`). So NO edge change is needed for `anth.us/newsroom/`: writing `newsroom/index.html` to the bucket serves it. The child task "edge check" verifies this read-only and records it; any change that did turn out to be needed is its own task and needs Ryan's approval before it is applied.
- Every other site's edge (`infra/edge/s3-projection-cms.yaml`; Shipped, Distinctive Mark, Data Parade, TI) routes `/newsroom*`, `/_next/*` and `/api/*` to the CMS Amplify app, so a `pages[]` path or section base `newsroom` there would be shadowed by the CMS. That is why the segment is per-site configuration. The docs task adds this to `docs/site-hosting.md`; a build-time check is not possible (projection does not know the edge), so the standard config refuses only the reserved prefixes it does know (`_data`, `_plugins`, `_papyrus`, `_next`, `api`) and documents `newsroom` as reserved on CMS-style edges.
- Projection itself treats no segment specially: `urls.basePath`, redirects and reconcile have no `newsroom` rule (`owns_page_key` only excludes `css/`, `assets/`, `_`-prefixed keys and `_data/knowledge/`).

### Seams for the future (not built now)
- Forum view: each thread gets `_data/home-page/threads/<key>.json` (messages in sequence) in the threads task, and a `threads` include links to a per-thread page path reserved as `homePage.threadBase` (default `conversations`); the page itself is the later epic.
- Public posting: Messages stay people-only; a public post would be a guest mutation (as reader-steering's `guest.mutations`) writing a Message with a reader identity (readerId/handle policy from reader-steering), moderated through `moderateMessage`. The export's author policy (`homePage.threads.authors`) is the single place that decides what is shown.
- Interactive publications: the published JSON files plus the islands runtime (`papyrus-islands.js`, `::island{}`) are the mount points; a `home-page` island reading `_data/home-page/*.json` is a later task.
- Public curation (Shipped reader-steering): the `recommended` selection is the natural place for reader votes to appear; the reader plugin's `subjects.json` can gain `reference:<key>` subjects later.

## Decisions recorded 2026-10-31 (Ryan)
1. Feature name: "home page" (identifiers above).
2. Authors on public Messages: opt-in public handles (`UserProfile.publicHandle`); no handle shows "Editor" / "AI"; no email, sub or UUID ever appears.
3. Cyclotron confidence: public, on the data and the cards, as a number with a label and a mark, never colour alone.
4. Reference fields: all fields except identity, full third-party text and attachments, and internal plumbing; explicit allowlist in code (privacy section).
5. Counts: configurable per component; defaults 6 per grid on the Anth.us page, 4 per section on the home of sections.
6. Selections: all three at launch, including recommended-not-yet-accepted; Anth.us's page uses all three.
7. Nav: `/newsroom/` goes into the Anth.us menu at launch (opt-in task).
8. Production: deploying this to production, including the first snapshot write to the Anth.us bucket, is approved; verification steps stay, approval gates are removed.

## Acceptance criteria for the epic
- With configuration only, a Papyrus site shows accepted References (and optionally recommended ones and Message threads) on public pages that interleave with Story listings; each Reference appears at most once per page.
- https://anth.us/newsroom/ is live from the standard projector; Anth.us's existing pages are byte-identical apart from a nav link if Ryan wants one.
- Changes to curation reach the public pages within one debounce window plus the edge lifetime, with no per-site code.
- No public page or data file contains an email, a person id, a Cognito sub or a UUID (reader-privacy scan in CI).
- Section index pages and a home of section blocks are available to every site as settings.
- Gherkin specs (narrative, complete) for every behaviour change; p.apyr.us documents the feature.
